summary:
FIRETRUST helps people compare NASA fire observations across changing satellites. Archives from MODIS (Terra and Aqua)
  and VIIRS (Suomi NPP) report different numbers for the same fires, so a jump in detections can reflect a new
  instrument, not more fire. FIRETRUST turns NASA FIRMS records into a monthly calendar of active cell days, using H3
  hexagons and UTC days, and puts MODIS on the Suomi NPP scale with a transparent seasonal ratio model.

  The app has five screens: Discover, Explore, Compare, Calendar and Evidence. Users can explore five regions (Portugal,
  Uruguay, Greece, Chile and Zambia), see recorded versus estimated activity, inspect monthly anomalies, trace every
  number to its NASA source file and hash, and export CSV or PNG.

  On a fixed test of Portugal and Uruguay for 2022 to 2025, the model cut mean absolute error against Suomi NPP by 52
  percent for Aqua (89.76 to 42.73) and 21 percent for Terra (100.83 to 80.06).

  We are careful about limits. Missing data stays unknown, never zero. Estimates measure agreement with another
  satellite, not true fire counts, burned area or future danger. Ground validation is still pending.
details:
NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellites observe the same fires but record different numbers because their instruments differ in pixel size and overpass time. When a long record switches from one satellite to another, the change can appear to be a surge in fire activity even when none occurred. FIRETRUST makes these differences visible and helps analysts make fairer comparisons.

FIRETRUST processes NASA FIRMS active fire records, covering 4,607,351 observations from 80 source batches with verified hashes. It measures activity through active cell days, counting unique H3 hexagons of approximately 5 km with at least one detection during a UTC day. It then estimates what VIIRS Suomi NPP would have recorded based on MODIS observations, using a seasonal ratio model with shrinkage. Tweedie and log linear models serve as comparators, while Terra and Aqua have separate registered models. Training uses data from 2012 to 2019, model selection uses 2020, and residual uncertainty bands are calibrated on 2021. Final evaluation uses complete years from 2022 to 2025, without randomly shuffling observations.

The web application includes five screens: Discover, Explore, Compare, Calendar and Evidence. Users can explore detections on a map, compare recorded and estimated activity, examine monthly calendars with missing data clearly identified, and review methods, benchmarks and source hashes. The application covers Portugal, Uruguay, Greece, Chile and Zambia, with CSV and PNG export options.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FIRETRUST helps researchers, journalists and land managers determine whether an apparent change in fire activity reflects a real trend or differences between satellite instruments. On the fixed test set, the error relative to Suomi NPP decreased by 52 percent for Aqua, from 89.76 to 42.73, and by 21 percent for Terra, from 100.83 to 80.06.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Scientific honesty is central to FIRETRUST's design. Recorded observations, model estimates and missing months are displayed differently, ensuring that missing data is never mistaken for zero activity. Estimates outside the calibrated range do not display uncertainty bands because reliable uncertainty estimates cannot be supported there.

The application also communicates known limitations, including systematic underprediction in certain regions. We evaluated recalibration for individual regions but found that it did not resolve the bias, so we chose not to include it. Our estimates measure agreement between satellite instruments rather than actual fire counts, burned area or future fire danger. Independent ground validation remains an important next step.

Tools and Technologies

The backend uses Python, FastAPI, DuckDB, H3, NumPy and Parquet. The frontend is built with React, TypeScript, Leaflet and Lucide. Testing uses Playwright and pytest, with 92 backend tests passing. The application is hosted on Vercel and uses NASA FIRMS data alongside a Natural Earth basemap.

Development was supported by OpenAI Codex, ChatGPT and Anthropic Claude Code for implementation, debugging, technical review and documentation. All reported scientific results were computed from NASA FIRMS observations and preserved evidence files.
